title: Best Honeywell Dehumidifier (2026): The TP Lineup Ranked
h1: The Best Honeywell Dehumidifiers for Your Home
dek: Honeywell's model names still use the old pint ratings, so a "70" is really a 50. Here's how to decode the TP lineup and pick the right one.
description: The best Honeywell dehumidifier for your home, from the smart TPFIT50AWK to the TP70PWKNR with pump, plus help with Honeywell manuals, filters and E3 codes.
intro: Honeywell is one of the most recognizable names in home comfort, and a Honeywell dehumidifier is often the first one shoppers reach for. Our top choice is the **TPFIT50AWK**, which earned a top score among large-capacity models in Consumer Reports' 2026 ratings and adds Wi-Fi and Alexa control to a well-proven design.

One thing to know up front: Honeywell doesn't build its own dehumidifiers. Since 2014, they've been engineered and manufactured under license by **JMATEK**, operating as Honeywell Air Comfort — the same brand-and-factory arrangement that has Midea building units for GE. And Honeywell's model names still reference pre-2019 pint ratings, so a "TP70" removes about 50 pints a day under today's DOE test.

We sorted the current TP lineup by the space each model suits, using DOE and ENERGY STAR data, manuals, published independent ratings and owner reviews. We've also included quick answers to the manual, filter and error-code questions Honeywell owners ask most.
topPicksLead: The **Honeywell TPFIT50AWK** is the best Honeywell dehumidifier for most homes, combining top independent ratings with Wi-Fi and Alexa control.

products.name: Honeywell Smart Wi-Fi Dehumidifier (TPFIT50AWK)
pros: Top-scoring large-capacity model in Consumer Reports' 2026 ratings
Wi-Fi app with Alexa voice control
Laundry mode and Auto-Comfort fan setting
cons: About 32 pints a day under the current DOE test, despite the "50" name
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you want one Honeywell backed by independent results rather than marketing, this is it. It pairs strong ratings with an app that lets you check humidity, schedule runs and get alerts without walking downstairs.
products.performance: It's rated at roughly 32 pints a day under the 2019 DOE procedure, which suits a damp basement, living area or large bedroom. Consumer Reports placed it at the top of its large-capacity group in 2026, and owners praise its quiet running and easy app setup. Laundry mode speeds up drying clothes on an indoor rack, and Auto-Comfort adjusts the fan to conditions. Thermal overload protection adds a measure of safety for long, unattended runs.

products.name: Honeywell 50-Pint Dehumidifier with Pump (TP70PWKNR)
pros: Built-in pump pushes water about 15 feet
50 pints a day under the current DOE test
Splash Guard tank cuts spills when emptying
Auto-defrost for cool basements and garages
cons: Costs more than the non-pump TP70WKN
Older TP70PWKN stock still on shelves can confuse shopping
products.whyWeLoveIt: If there's nowhere convenient to run a gravity hose — a below-grade corner, a room with no drain — the pump lifts water to a laundry sink or out a window so the unit runs unattended.
products.performance: This eco-refrigerant "R" version has replaced the original TP70PWKN at Honeywell's own store, though some retailers are still selling through older stock. Both remove about 50 pints a day under the DOE test, and the pump pushes condensate roughly 15 feet vertically or horizontally. Auto-defrost keeps it working in cooler spaces. Compare it against pump models from other brands in our [best dehumidifier with pump](/best/best-dehumidifier-with-pump/) guide.
products.notes: Check the exact model number on the listing; TP70PWKN and TP70PWKNR are close siblings but not identical.

products.name: Honeywell 20-Pint ENERGY STAR Dehumidifier (TP30WKN)
pros: Rated for spaces up to about 2,000 sq ft
cons: Too small for a wet basement
products.whyWeLoveIt: Honeywell's 50-pint models are overkill for a single damp bedroom or home office. The TP30WKN handles that smaller job with less cost, less floor space and ENERGY STAR efficiency.
products.performance: It's rated at about 20 pints a day under the 2019 DOE test — the "30" refers to the old rating. Honeywell says it suits spaces up to roughly 2,000 sq ft, though a single room is its sweet spot. If you'd like app control, the TP30AWKNR adds Wi-Fi and Alexa for a modest premium. See how it compares in our [best small dehumidifier](/best/best-small-dehumidifier/) picks.

products.name: Honeywell 50-Pint Smart Wi-Fi Dehumidifier (TP70AWKNR)
pros: 50 pints a day under the DOE test
Wi-Fi app and Alexa with empty-tank alerts
products.whyWeLoveIt: Want app alerts and remote control in a big basement that already has a floor drain? The TP70AWKNR gives you Honeywell's largest capacity with smart features and skips the pump you don't need.
products.performance: It shares the same 50-pint hardware as the pump model and is rated for roughly 4,000 sq ft, the largest coverage in Honeywell's current range. The app lets you schedule runs and get a notification before the tank fills. If you won't use the app, the non-smart TP70WKN removes the same amount of water for less. For other connected units, see our [best Wi-Fi dehumidifier](/best/best-wifi-dehumidifier/) roundup.

sections.heading: How we pick the best Honeywell dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't run a lab. We translated every model's name into its DOE 2019 rating using ENERGY STAR and manufacturer data, compared drainage, smart features and warranty terms from the manuals, and checked the CPSC database for recalls. We weighed published independent ratings, including Consumer Reports, and read owner reviews to see how the units hold up after the first season — including how warranty claims are handled.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Honeywell dehumidifier

items.label: The real pint rating
items.text: Subtract the marketing: TP30 is about 20 pints, TP50 about 32 and TP70 about 50 under today's DOE test. Our [size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) helps you match that to your space.

items.label: Pump or gravity
items.text: Pay for the TP70PWKNR only if there's no floor drain or low sink within hose reach.

items.label: Smart features you'll use
items.text: The "A" in TP70AWKNR, TP30AWKNR and TPFIT50AWK signals Wi-Fi and Alexa. Worth it for basements; optional for a bedroom.

items.label: The exact model number
items.text: The newer "R" eco-refrigerant versions are replacing older stock. Confirm what the listing is actually selling.

items.label: A plan for the hose
items.text: Owners often find the included drain hose flimsy. A sturdier garden hose of the right length is an inexpensive upgrade.

sections.heading: Honeywell dehumidifier warranty, manual and repair help

blocks.text: Honeywell's five-year limited sealed-system warranty is generous on paper. The recurring complaint in owner reviews is what happens around and after it: slow service turnaround and costly out-of-warranty labor. Register your unit, keep the receipt and photograph the model label.
Look for the model number on the label on the back or side of the unit, then search it on the Honeywell Air Comfort (JMATEK) support site to download the user manual and error-code table.

items: Unplug the unit and slide out the washable filter, usually behind the rear or front grille.
Vacuum loose dust, then rinse in lukewarm water.
Let it dry completely before reinstalling; a damp filter can harbor mildew.
**No water collecting:** the room may already be at your setpoint, or the coils may be icing in a cool room. See our [not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/) guide.
**Error code on the display:** unplug for 10 minutes, restart and check the manual's table.
**Unit won't start:** confirm the tank is seated correctly and the outlet works.
**Leaking:** check that the drain hose is secure and sloping downward.

blocks.text: The **Honeywell TPFIT50AWK** is the best Honeywell dehumidifier for most homes, thanks to top independent ratings and genuinely useful smart features. Choose the **TP70PWKNR** if you need a pump, the **TP30WKN** for a single room and the **TP70AWKNR** for app control in a large basement with a drain. Just compare DOE ratings rather than model names, and see our [Frigidaire vs. Honeywell](/compare/frigidaire-vs-honeywell-dehumidifier/) comparison for how the "70" stacks up against a true 50-pint rival.

faqs.q: What is the best Honeywell dehumidifier?
faqs.a: For most homes, the TPFIT50AWK, which earned a top large-capacity score in Consumer Reports' 2026 ratings and adds Wi-Fi and Alexa control. Choose the TP70PWKNR if you need a built-in pump, or the TP30WKN for a single room.
They're engineered and built under license by JMATEK, which sells them as Honeywell Air Comfort and has made Honeywell-branded dehumidifiers since 2014. Honeywell itself licenses the name.

faqs.q: Is the Honeywell TP50WK a true 50-pint dehumidifier?
faqs.a: No. Honeywell's model numbers use the older test standard. The TP50 models remove roughly 32 pints a day under the current DOE test; for true 50-pint capacity, look at the TP70 models.

faqs.q: What does E3 mean on a Honeywell dehumidifier?
faqs.a: E-codes on Honeywell units point to a sensor or component fault, and the exact meaning varies by model. Unplug the unit for about 10 minutes and restart it; if the code returns, check the error table in your manual and contact Honeywell Air Comfort support, especially while you're under warranty.

faqs.q: Can a Honeywell portable air conditioner with dehumidifier mode replace a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Not really. A portable AC's dry mode removes some moisture while it cools, but it's designed to lower temperature, not hold a humidity setpoint. For a damp basement or a room that's cool but clammy, a dedicated dehumidifier does the job far better. Our [dehumidifier vs. air conditioner](/guides/dehumidifier-vs-air-conditioner/) guide explains the difference.

Drying performance is well regarded and the sealed system carries a five-year limited warranty. The most common owner complaints concern slow warranty service and costly repairs once coverage ends, plus a flimsy stock drain hose.
